# pkc/util

> pkc helpers: errors as values, and Go-compatible number parsing (prefix u_).

truck [pkc](../pkc.md) · [source](../../../registry/pkc/util.pkg)

`pkc` reports errors through the global `pk_err`: a failing function
sets it, usually with `u_fail`, and returns `null` or `false`, and the
caller passes the failure on. `u_atoi` parses numbers the way Go's
`strconv.Atoi` does, so that `pkc` accepts what the Go compiler accepts.

The general string and vector helpers `pkc` uses everywhere (`str_trim`,
`str_fields`, `str_split`, `str_join`, `str_quote`, `vec_get_str`, ...)
live in [rt/str](../rt/str.md) and [rt/vec](../rt/vec.md), where every
program can use them.

## Library code

Merged into every program that uses this package.

```
// pk_err holds the message of the most recent error.
global pk_err: str = ""

fn u_fail(msg: str) -> bool
  pk_err = msg
  return false
end

// u_atoi parses like strconv.Atoi: an optional sign, then digits.
fn u_atoi(s: str, ok: ptr bool) -> int
  if len(s) > 0 && s[0] == '+'
    return str_parse_int(str_slice(s, 1, len(s)), ok)
  end
  return str_parse_int(s, ok)
end
```
